item.title: France braces for more protests – security measures at a glance
item.description: After a weekend of protests, riots and looting, France is looking to head off further unrest, ahead of fresh demonstrations called for Saturday. Here are some of the measures authorities have ordered: – Curfews – Partial nighttime curfews were imposed in parts of Paris and several other cities on Monday and Tuesday nights, applied to areas where clashes broke out last weekend and shopping zones that had been targeted by looters. Paris also banned public gatherings on the Champs Elysees, near major public buildings, and near train stations. Marseille, France’s second-biggest city, has banned unaccompanied minors from central shopping streets every night up to and including Friday. – Bans – Paris police have banned people carrying bottles or cans of petrol or gas, or possessing fireworks, up to and including Thursday. Last weekend, youths set fire to several shops and public buildings, and shot fireworks through tubes at police, wounding several. – Deployment – French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu has vowed a “massive” security deployment for Saturday, after his government admitted it “lost control” last weekend. President Emmanuel Macron on Sunday said authorities would be “uncompromising” towards “agitators from ultra-left fringe groups” that he blamed for much of the violence. Elite police units have been mobilised for the coming weekend. Macron has not, however, declared a state of emergency that would allow troops to be sent to reinforce police lines. However, soldiers who for more than a decade have been patrolling sensitive sites, airports and train stations and tourist zones under “Operation Sentinelle” would continue to be deployed to protect those spots. – Shops – The government has announced interest-free loans for 3,000 shops that were damaged, many of them looted, during last weekend’s unrest. Shop owners say that is not enough, though. Crowdfunding initiatives have sprung up on social media for residents to help their local shops rebuild. But the total amount being raised is only in the low hundreds of thousands of euros — whereas the sector says the damage bill will run to hundreds of millions. – Burnt bikes – Tourists visiting Paris right now hoping to use the usually ubiquitous rental bikes available via apps might find them a bit more scarce. More than 1,000 of the 40,000 bicycles deployed across the capital were destroyed, often burned, as they were thrown into makeshift street barricades built by protesters, according to an AFP tally of figures from the operators. – Food deliveries – Staying in and ordering food delivery could also be a problem for some. The Union-Independants union covering most delivery bike riders has asked Uber Eats, Deliveroo and other such companies to suspend deliveries to areas considered dangerous. It called for the riders to be able to cancel deliveries without losing money and for them to have a system allowing them to see risky areas in real time. item.title: Student loans voluntary, not compulsory, NELFUND tells tertiary institutions
item.description: … Fund says borrowing is voluntary, urges institutions to stop misleading students By Joseph Erunke, Abuja The Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND) has declared that no student in Nigeria’s tertiary institutions is under any obligation to apply for a student loan, insisting that the scheme is designed to assist those facing financial hardship, not compel every student to borrow. The Fund, in a clarification issued on Wednesday, stressed that accessing the interest-free loan remains a personal decision that must be guided by a student’s financial circumstances and genuine need for assistance. NELFUND’s position comes amid the need to ensure that students, tertiary institutions and other stakeholders clearly understand the purpose and conditions of the federal government’s student loan initiative. The Fund explained that the scheme was established to break financial barriers to higher education and prevent eligible Nigerian students from abandoning their academic ambitions because of a lack of funds. It, however, cautioned against any interpretation or practice that could make borrowing compulsory for students, irrespective of their financial capacity. According to the Fund, compelling students who do not need financial assistance to take loans would defeat the very purpose of the programme. “The objective is not to encourage every student to borrow, but to ensure that every eligible Nigerian student who genuinely needs financial assistance has the opportunity to access it,” NELFUND said. It added that the loan scheme was a support mechanism rather than an obligation, stressing that students who could independently meet their educational expenses were free to pursue their studies without applying for the facility. Beyond clarifying the voluntary nature of the scheme, NELFUND reminded prospective beneficiaries that the interest-free facility carries repayment obligations under the provisions of the Student Loans Act. The Fund, therefore, urged students to familiarise themselves with the terms and conditions governing the loans and make informed decisions before submitting applications. While describing the scheme as a critical intervention to expand access to higher education, NELFUND maintained that its priority remained ensuring that financial difficulties did not prevent qualified Nigerian students from pursuing their educational aspirations. The Fund also called on tertiary institutions, student leaders and other stakeholders to provide accurate information about the programme and guide students appropriately, particularly those struggling to finance their education. It reiterated its commitment to ensuring that eligible students who genuinely require financial assistance could access the facility without being misled into believing that taking a loan was a compulsory condition for studying in a Nigerian tertiary institution. item.title: Regulator has ‘power’ to force Man city sale if charges upheld
item.description: English football’s Independent Regulator (IFR) will have “absolute power” to force Manchester City’s owners to sell if they are ultimately found to have run the club improperly, the watchdog’s chair has said. Premier League leaders City have been found guilty on over 100 charges of breaking Premier League financial rules by an independent commission between 2009 and 2018. The club have appealed and deny any wrongdoing, but face a severe sanction unless they overturn the verdict. Owned by Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed al-Nahyan, vice-president and deputy prime minister of the United Arab Emirates, City have blossomed into the dominant force in English football since a 2008 takeover. “We have the power to ask an owner to step away from a club if we believe that they run a club in a way that is neither fit, fair or done with propriety,” the IFR’s chair David Kogan told “The Rest is Football” podcast. Asked if an owner could refuse to divest, Kogan added: “No. We’ve got absolute power to do so.” Kogan also said last week he would resign if there is any political interference in any investigation the IFR may undertake into City. British Prime Minister Andy Burnham has come under criticism for his initial comments on City’s guilty verdict, saying he would be “really concerned” if the club’s Abu Dhabi owners left the club following the verdict. Downing Street subsequently had to backtrack, insisting no one was “above the rules”. Burnham, who was mayor of Greater Manchester from 2017 to June 2026, has since published all of his dealings with the City hierarchy. But the case poses a delicate balancing act for the UK government in preserving its longstanding ties with the Emirates without interfering in the independence of the disciplinary action against City. item.title: Ebola: NCDC urges calm, strengthens FCT surveillance
item.description: The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) has urged Nigerians to remain calm and rely on verified information following the confirmation of an Ebola disease case in the Federal Capital Territory. The agency disclosed this in a post on its X platform on Wednesday, saying the Federal Government, through the NCDC and relevant health authorities, was strengthening surveillance and response efforts. The NCDC explained that Ebola spreads through direct contact with the blood or body fluids of an infected person who is sick or has died, as well as contact with contaminated materials. It urged members of the public to report suspected cases promptly, stressing that early reporting was critical to saving lives. The agency advised Nigerians to seek information from credible sources and avoid spreading unverified reports about the outbreak. item.title: Omokri receives Mexico’s agreement as Nigeria’s Ambassador
item.description: Reno Omokri has received the agreement of the Government of Mexico for his appointment as Nigeria’s Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary to the country. Omokri disclosed this on his X platform on Wednesday, saying the Chargé d’Affaires of the Embassy of Mexico in Abuja, Mr José Manuel Briseño Flores, delivered the agreement to the Director of Protocol at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Ambassador Babagana Wakil. The agreement formally signifies the Mexican government’s acceptance of Omokri’s appointment as Nigeria’s ambassador to Mexico. According to Omokri, his diplomatic assignment will also include concurrent accreditation to Guatemala, Honduras and Nicaragua. He announced the development in a post expressing gratitude to God, describing himself by his full name, Bemigho Reno Omokri, and confirming his designation as Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of the Federal Republic of Nigeria to the United Mexican States. item.title: 2027: APC campaign council reshuffles youth, women mobilisation teams
item.description: The PBAT/APC 2027 Presidential Campaign Council has announced changes to its leadership structure, including the creation of a directorate to oversee stage organisation and management ahead of the general elections. Imo State Governor and council secretary, Hope Uzodimma, announced the appointments in a statement on Monday, saying the changes were designed to improve coordination, strengthen the council’s structure and boost operational efficiency. Under the new arrangement, Farouk Aliyu will head the Directorate of Stage Organisation and Management, with Adejare Bello appointed as co-director. The council also named Youth Development Minister Ayodele Olawande as director of youth mobilisation, while Dayo Israel will serve as his deputy. For women mobilisation, Mary Aille Idele was appointed director, with Betta Edu as deputy director and Imaan Suleman as secretary. Uzodimma said the appointments were part of efforts to establish a coordinated and inclusive campaign structure capable of mobilising support for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027. He said the appointees were expected to deploy their experience and organisational skills to their respective roles and collaborate with other directorates in implementing the council’s campaign and mobilisation plans. The changes come as the ruling All Progressives Congress prepares for the 2027 presidential election, with youth and women mobilisation identified as key components of its campaign strategy. item.title: Zamfara 2027: Governor Lawal, 14 other candidates sign peace accord
item.description: Governor Dauda Lawal of Zamfara State and 14 other governorship candidates yesterday signed a peace accord to ensure peace and order in the forthcoming 2027 General elections. The accord, organised by the Zamfara State Police Command in Gusau, was signed at the Peace Accord and Election Security Summit held in Zamfara State. The Peace Accord signing ceremony was meant to ensure peace and order for all political parties in the country as a preparation for free and fair 2027 elections. Governor Lawal, along with all contestants in the governorship, national and state assembly elections, were invited to sign and promise that no one will violate or work against any election processes before, during and after elections. The governor, as one of the contestants under the All Progressive Congress (APC), signed the accord and prayed for peace, free and fair elections, and all the political parties did the same. In his speech, Zamfara State Commissioner of Police, CP Ahmed Mohammed Bello Daga, called on all the contestants to shun, avoid, and not try to violate any election processes before, during and after elections. He warned that any political aspirant or member of any political party found violating the law will be decisively trailed and charged before the court of law. Also, the Deputy Commissioner of Police, Zamfara State Command, Kabir Abdul Randawa, has assured political parties and residents of the command’s commitment to providing adequate security and ensuring peaceful political activities in the state. He urged all political parties and candidates to shun intimidation, violence and other acts capable of threatening the peace. item.title: NMA raises alarm over doctors’ health, burnout
item.description: By Chinedu Adonu The Nigerian Medical Association (NMA), Enugu State chapter, has called for improved working conditions and greater attention to doctors’ welfare, warning that medical practitioners risk compromising their own health while caring for patients. The state Chairman of the association, Dr Ortuanya Emeka, made the call in Enugu during a press briefing to mark the 2026 Physicians’ Week celebration. Ortuanya said the theme of the celebration, “Saving the Savers — Promoting Physicians’ Well-being and Preventing Burnout, Cardiovascular Disease, and Premature Death,” highlighted the challenges confronting medical practitioners. He said the future of medicine depended not only on professional commitment but also on a healthy and motivated workforce, supportive government policies, adequate healthcare infrastructure, quality medical education and the responsible adoption of modern technology. According to him, doctors routinely work long hours, handle emergencies, make critical decisions and bear the emotional burden of human suffering, often under difficult working conditions. “Unfortunately, most times, if not at all times, we become so committed to our duties to the point of neglecting our own lives,” he said. The NMA chairman stressed that physicians’ well-being should be treated as a practical professional priority rather than an issue discussed only during ceremonial occasions. He urged Governor Peter Mbah, through the Commissioner for Health, Prof. George Ugwu, to strengthen advocacy for safe working conditions and create an environment where doctors could deliver quality healthcare without unnecessary occupational risks. “We must encourage healthcare employers and relevant authorities to recognise that an exhausted workforce cannot be expected to function indefinitely at its best,” he said. Ortuanya also condemned violence against healthcare workers, describing threats, intimidation, harassment and physical attacks on doctors as unacceptable. He said hospitals should provide safe environments for both patients and healthcare professionals, warning that insecurity in medical facilities could undermine effective healthcare delivery. “Our hospitals must be places of healing, not environments in which healthcare professionals fear for their safety,” he said. The NMA chairman further called for sustained engagement with relevant authorities to address issues affecting medical practitioners, including remuneration, career progression, workplace safety, training opportunities and the availability of essential resources. He said improving doctors’ welfare and working conditions was essential to sustaining a motivated medical workforce and ensuring quality healthcare delivery. item.title: 2027: DSS uncovers plot against NYSC members, arrests suspects – INEC
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission INEC, Prof. Joash Amupitan SAN, has disclosed that the people behind a plot against the Commission’s Ad Hoc staff, especially Youth Corps members, have been uncovered and arrested and would be prosecuted soon. Prof. Amupitan made the disclosure in Enugu at the South-East Zonal Interactive Meeting with Staff and Readiness Assessment for the 2027 General Election. According to the Commission’s Daily Bulletin, INEC recently identified potential risks to its Ad Hoc staff, “especially Youth Corps members,” and has taken measures to neutralise the threat. He said the people behind the plot were uncovered by the Department of State Services DSS. The INEC Chairman added that the Commission plans to host a Security Conference “very soon” to address other issues relating to election security. On the Commission’s wider security arrangements, he said its partnership with the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security (ICCES) had been reinvigorated and expanded. Prof. Amupitan said INEC was working with security agencies at national and state levels, using its Election Risk Management ERM tools, to develop “a robust, intelligence-driven security architecture.” He also identified a lingering public trust deficit, voter apathy and the rising tide of misinformation and disinformation as the Commission’s greatest challenges. “A single malicious fake news post, an unverified rumour, or a deepfake video can travel across millions of screens in seconds,” he warned. He said false narratives only gain traction when the Commission’s administrative execution falters. “The conduct, competence, and character of our staff in the field are either our strongest defence against fake news, or its biggest catalyst,” he stated. The INEC Chairman said the Commission’s response would be “proactive transparency, swift official communication, and uncompromising operational precision at every polling unit.” On discipline, Prof. Amupitan said, “Partisan leaning, administrative negligence, extortion, or compromised ethics will not be tolerated under my leadership.” He reminded staff that Section 26 of the Electoral Act 2026 requires all staff, Electoral Officers, Presiding Officers, Returning Officers and participating security officials to swear an oath of loyalty and neutrality. “The question governing your actions must never be ‘Who will benefit from this decision?’ The question must always be ‘What does the law require me to do?'” he said. item.title: Ebola: Avoid unnecessary physical contact, Academy of Medical Sciences cautions
item.description: By Sola Ogundipe The Academy of Medical Sciences of Nigeria has urged Nigerians to be wary of handshakes, hugs and other unnecessary physical contact and to adopt non-contact greetings instead as part of the immediate nationwide high alert response to the confirmed Ebola case in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Abuja. In a public health advisory issued on Tuesday, the Academy endorsed the Federal Government’s response to the confirmed case involving a woman who recently arrived in Nigeria from Uganda, the Academy commended the prompt isolation of the patient, commencement of contact tracing and intensified surveillance. Noting that the measure was an additional precaution members of the public were urged to wash their hands regularly with soap and water or use alcohol-based hand sanitisers, avoid contact with the body fluids of sick persons and refrain from handling the bodies of people suspected to have died from Ebola. The advisory, jointly signed by the Academy’s President, Emeritus Professor Osato Giwa-Osagie; Foundation President, Professor Oladapo A. Ashiru; and Rapid Response Committee member, Professor Boaz Adegboro, urged the federal government to extend heightened preparedness measures across the country, drawing on Nigeria’s successful containment of Ebola in 2014 and its response to the COVID-19 pandemic. Nigeria’s Ebola Outbreak Explained Nigeria’s experience with Ebola Nigeria’s experience with Ebola in 2014 demonstrated how quickly an imported infection could become a national public health emergency in a country with a large population and busy international travel routes. On July 20, 2014, Patrick Sawyer, a Liberian-American diplomat who was infected with Ebola, arrived at Murtala Muhammed International Airport in Lagos from Liberia. He was subsequently admitted to a private hospital, where his illness was initially difficult to distinguish from other diseases. He died on July 25, 2014. His arrival triggered an emergency response involving the Federal Ministry of Health, the Lagos State Government, the NCDC and international health partners. According to a report published in the United States Centres for Disease Control and Prevention’s Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report, Nigeria recorded 20 Ebola cases, comprising 19 laboratory-confirmed cases and one probable case, by September 24, 2014. Eight fatalities from seven laboratory-confirmed Ebola and one probable case were recorded. The deaths included Sawyer and Dr Ameyo Stella Adadevoh, who placed the foreigner in quarantine, as well as six others who were infected during the chain of transmission that followed his arrival. The outbreak was eventually contained, with no new cases reported after August 31, 2014. The country identified and monitored 894 contacts during the response, while 11 patients with laboratory-confirmed Ebola were discharged from care. How prepared is the country for Ebola? Nigeria’s latest preparedness efforts began before the reported FCT case. On June 9, 2026, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu approved the immediate release of N10 billion as emergency intervention funding for public health preparedness and response. The fund is separate from a N21.2 million per-state disbursement under the State Outbreak Investigation and Response Fund. The Presidency also announced the establishment of a Presidential Task Force on Ebola Virus Disease Preparedness and Emerging Public Health Threats, chaired by the Chief of Staff to the President, Femi Gbajabiamila. According to the State House, the fund was intended to strengthen the operational capacity of the NCDC and support critical national public health emergency response activities. The government also directed states hosting international airports and international border corridors, alongside relevant ministries, departments and agencies, to submit their preparedness plans, funding requirements and intervention needs. The measures announced included intensified passenger screening at international airports, enhanced monitoring of passengers arriving through designated high-risk routes, and the activation of referral and isolation centres at the Lagos and Abuja international airports. Other proposed measures included health declaration systems for passengers arriving from or transiting through designated high-risk countries and improved coordination among health, immigration, aviation and security authorities. item.title: London/Paris Club refunds: Court voids EFCC probe report
item.description: …Faults FG over probe of ALGON lawyer By Ikechukwu Nnochiri ABUJA—A High Court of the Federal Capital Territory, FCT, sitting in Garki, yesterday, set aside an investigation report by the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission, EFCC, which alleged fraud in the London/Paris Club refunds involving the 774 local government areas in the country. In the judgment, Justice Suleiman Belgore faulted the Federal Government for directing the anti-graft agency to investigate the matter despite two separate court decisions. The judge held that the Federal Government acted beyond its powers by directing the EFCC, through the Office of the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, to investigate court judgments ordering payment to a consultant, Dr. Ted Iseghohi-Edwards, for legal services rendered in the matter. Justice Belgore noted that the directive came after the government had issued promissory notes for the payment following a clearance report by the Department of State Services, DSS. He held that the EFCC’s subsequent report amounted to an affront to the authority of the court. “The law and the court must be respected. They are both official and statutory. It is not within the powers of the Respondents to use Exhibit GG to impugn the integrity of the court by claiming the judgement was obtained fraudulently,” he held. The judge said the appropriate course for the Federal Government was to file processes seeking to set aside the judgments rather than investigate them. “There were negotiated terms of engagement between the Incorporated Trustees of ALGON and the applicant. These terms of engagement were renegotiated by parties in open court on September 15, 2016,” Justice Belgore added. He held that the 10 promissory notes issued to Iseghohi-Edwards in compliance with a valid order of mandamus made against the Federal Government by the Federal High Court were validly issued by former President Muhammadu Buhari. Consequently, the court upheld the suit filed by the Abuja-based lawyer, holding that there was unassailable evidence that he was retained by the Incorporated Trustees of the Association of Local Governments of Nigeria, ALGON, to represent the 774 local government areas in the London/Paris Club refunds matter. Among the reliefs granted, the court barred the Federal Government and its agencies from arresting, detaining or prosecuting the plaintiff, or infringing on his fundamental rights in connection with the matter.
